title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 219: Secrets of the Annual Ring
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 219 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Secrets of the Annual Ring: Dendroclimatology and Volcanic Cataclysms

Paragraph 1. When you cut a tree trunk, you can see many round wooden rings inside. In places with cold winters, a tree stops growing during winter and makes exactly one new ring every year. When spring and summer are warm and rainy, the tree grows fast and makes a wide ring. When the weather is very cold or dry, the tree makes a very thin ring.

Paragraph 2. Scientists compare rings from living old trees with wooden beams from old buildings and ruins. Using this method, they have built weather records going back over ten thousand years. Sometimes, scientists find broken wood cells inside a ring, called a 'frost ring'. A frost ring happens when a sudden summer freeze hits trees during their warm growing months.

Paragraph 3. Old history books talk about a scary dark sky in the year 536 CE. In Europe, the sun looked weak like the moon for an entire year, and summer snow fell in China, ruining food crops. Scientist Dr. Michael Baillie studied ancient pine trees in California and proved that huge volcanic eruptions caused this long cold shock. Giant volcanoes threw gas high into the sky, blocking warm sunlight and cooling the Earth for years.

Paragraph 4. To check these volcanic dates, scientists also study deep ice taken from Greenland and Antarctica. Dust from ancient volcanoes fell onto polar snow and stayed trapped in ice layers. Together, tree rings and polar ice prove that global warming over the last fifty years is much faster than normal natural changes in the past.

groups.title: Questions 1–4
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

q1.text: How many rings does a tree in a cold-winter area normally grow each year?

steps: Đoạn 1: Cây tạo chính xác 1 vòng mới mỗi năm (one new ring every year).

q2.text: What causes a 'frost ring' inside a tree?
options: A. Forest fires burning the outer bark
B. A sudden freeze during warm summer months
C. Heavy rain washing soil off tree roots
D. Insects eating through wooden beams

steps: Đoạn 2: Băng giá bất ngờ ập xuống giữa mùa hè (sudden summer freeze).

q3.text: What caused the terrible dark weather in 536 CE?
options: A. Massive volcanic eruptions blocking sunlight
B. A large rock falling into the Pacific Ocean
C. Smoke from thousands of city factories
D. Cold ocean winds blowing from California

steps: Đoạn 3: Các vụ phun trào núi lửa khổng lồ (huge volcanic eruptions).

q4.text: Besides tree rings, what else do scientists study to verify ancient volcanoes?
options: A. Deep ocean sand near Europe
B. Old metal coins from ruins
C. Deep ice layers from Greenland and Antarctica
D. Broken glass found inside caves

steps: Đoạn 4: Nghiên cứu băng sâu lấy từ Greenland và Nam Cực.

q5.text: Over half of the population in China died during the cold year of 536 CE.

steps: Đoạn 3: Chỉ nói tuyết rơi mùa hè làm hỏng mùa màng, không nêu tỷ lệ dân số tử vong.

q6.text: Trees usually produce wider rings when spring and summer are warm and wet.

steps: Đoạn 1: Mùa xuân hè ấm và nhiều mưa giúp cây tạo vòng gỗ rộng (wide ring).

q7.text: Volcanic gas in the sky made the Earth much warmer after 536 CE.

steps: Đoạn 3: Che nắng và làm Trái Đất lạnh đi (cooling the Earth), không phải nóng lên.

q8.text: Recent global warming is identical in speed to natural weather cycles in the past.

steps: Đoạn 4: Sự nóng lên 50 năm qua nhanh hơn nhiều so với biến đổi tự nhiên trước kia.
